title: The Guest
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, foggy small American town, cold blue and amber tones, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, no text, no watermark
caption:
Final part. The Mercers never vanished. They were working. 🕯️

Original fiction. New series tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: in the abandoned Mercer house, Jenna found one locked door. At 3:12, someone knocked. From the inside.
scenes.image: an old bedroom door in darkness, a young woman with a flashlight frozen in front of it

scenes.narration: The deadbolt turned. The door swung open. And Tom and Ruth Mercer stood in the doorway, exactly as they were in 1987.
scenes.image: a man and a woman in 1980s pajamas standing in an open bedroom doorway, pale and calm, lit by cold light

scenes.narration: Same pajamas. Same faces. Not one day older. Ruth smiled like a neighbor. You must be the one who locks her door.
scenes.image: close-up of a gentle 1980s woman's face smiling in cold light, her eyes far too still

scenes.narration: Tom spoke softly. We didn't vanish. We were hired. Every night we walk ahead of it and open the doors, so it never has to stop.
scenes.image: a man in pajamas walking through a dark house holding a door open, a long tall shadow stretching behind him

scenes.narration: Jenna asked the only question left. Protecting the town from what? Ruth looked almost sorry. Sweetheart. Nobody's protecting anybody.
scenes.image: young woman and an older woman face to face in a dark hallway, only the flashlight between them

scenes.narration: An open door isn't a shield. It's a welcome. Every night the Guest walks through town and takes a little. An hour. A memory. A year. Mrs. Pruitt's list was never a record. It's a menu.
scenes.image: a leather ledger open on a table by an oil lamp, faded handwritten ink, a long shadow falling across the pages

scenes.narration: And a locked door? To the Guest, that isn't no. It's an invitation. It means come in. And stay.
scenes.image: a brass deadbolt on a front door glowing faintly, as if warmed from the other side

scenes.narration: Behind Jenna, every door slammed shut. Tom held out a ring of old keys. Somebody has to open the doors. We've been waiting so long to rest.
scenes.image: a man's hand holding out a ring of old brass keys in a dark hallway, every door behind him shut

scenes.narration: Now, if you play the Mercer tape backwards, you'll hear a new voice. A young woman. Patient. Counting doors. Her name is Jenna.
scenes.image: an empty farmhouse hallway at 3 AM, every door open, a young woman's silhouette walking away into fog

scenes.narration: Tomorrow night: a roadside motel, a night clerk, and one rule. Never rent Room 9.
scenes.image: lonely roadside motel at night in the rain, a single lit window at the end of a row of doors
